description: Tick-normalized height-mode time-lock vectors: nLockTime, nSequence, and coinbase maturity. T(x) is the cumulative tick of block x, inclusive of its own interval, from the schedule. Height-mode predicates: nLockTime is strict and absolute — final in block b iff T(b) > 600*lockTime; nSequence is weak and relative — mature in block b iff T(b) - T(fundingBlock) >= 600*relativeLock; coinbase maturity is weak and absolute — spendable in block b iff T(b) - T(creationBlock) >= 60,000. Mempool forms use T(tip+1) from the schedule, never T(tip)+tau(tip). BCHN escape clauses: nLockTime==0 is final everywhere; every-input-SEQUENCE_FINAL is final regardless of nLockTime. A coinbase transaction is exempt from both predicates, but only from H_a + 1 onward: at or before H_a both fields bind and the coinbase is evaluated like any other transaction. The exemption is a scope restriction on the predicates, so it lives in the caller behind the same upgrade predicate the rest of the rule set uses; the coinbase vectors model that short circuit via `subjectIsCoinbase`, gated on the upgrade boundary at H_a + 1, and lock_noncoinbase_bip54_twin pins that an identical non-coinbase is still bound. Coinbase maturity is unaffected, because it reads the spent output's height and a coinbase spends none. The time-mode comparison and the LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD split are unchanged. `vectors` holds the height-mode vectors: no row there carries a blockTime, the time-mode arm is evaluated with block time 0 (so every time-mode locktime is treated as not yet reached), and releaseBlock is always a decimal string. `timeModeVectors` is a separate list with the same row layout plus `args.blockTime`, which applies only there: the value the time-mode arm compares against (final iff lockTime < blockTime), supplied unchanged at every block and mempool check of that vector. Under BIP 113 a node passes the median-time-past of the evaluated block's parent (for the mempool, of the tip) there, not the block's own timestamp. In these vectors the exemption gate is by height (b > H_a) and independent of blockTime, whereas a node derives both from the same median-time-past; a consumer must set its activation gate separately from the cutoff. The supplied 1,800,000,000 is before activation for an activation time of 15 May 2027 (1,810,382,400, mainnet); a consumer that derives its activation gate from the same time must use parameters whose activation time is later than the cutoff (so not chipnet's earlier activation time, 1,794,744,000), or set the gate by height as these vectors do. It is not the cutoff a chain has at H_a + 1, which is why the rows that pin the exemption use an nLockTime far past activation. In `timeModeVectors` releaseBlock is the smallest block at which the predicate holds given that constant blockTime, or null if it holds at no block. Every expected value is a hand-derived golden pin; the generator verifies the shared reference evaluators (timelock_ticks.h) against the pins and refuses to emit on any mismatch. All integer values are decimal strings to preserve full 64-bit precision.

vectors.name: lock_escape_zero
vectors.note: nLockTime==0 is final at every block via the BCHN escape, even with a non-final input sequence

vectors.name: lock_escape_all_seqfinal
vectors.note: absolute nLockTime is a no-op when every input is SEQUENCE_FINAL; the CHIP example release at 1,000,111 only holds with a non-final sequence

vectors.name: lock_pre_L1
vectors.note: strict: T(b) > 600 means T(1)=600 is still non-final

vectors.name: lock_pre_L100
vectors.note: legacy release block = L+1

vectors.name: seq_pre_n1_c100
vectors.note: weak: equality at c+n satisfies

vectors.name: seq_pre_n6_c100
vectors.note: legacy release block = c+n

vectors.name: mat_pre_c0
vectors.note: genesis coinbase: 60,000 ticks = 100 blocks

vectors.name: mat_pre_c500000
vectors.note: legacy release block = c+100

vectors.name: lock_post_doc
vectors.note: CHIP example: nLocktime=1,000,011 releases at block 1,000,111, the first block whose tick exceeds 600*1,000,011 = 600,006,600

vectors.name: lock_post_600grid
vectors.note: strictness where 600*L (600,006,000) is exactly a block tick (block 1,000,100)

vectors.name: lock_post_Ha
vectors.note: lock naming the activation height releases at the first 1-minute block; L <= H_a keeps release = L+1

vectors.name: lock_post_pre_Ha
vectors.note: pre-activation lock: release = L+1 exactly as legacy, because blocks <= H_a are 600-tick

vectors.name: seq_post_fund_Ha_n1
vectors.note: one normalized unit (600 ticks) = ten 1-minute blocks; mempool MUST use T(tip+1) from the schedule, not T(tip)+tau(tip)

vectors.name: seq_post_n1_c1000010
vectors.note: post-activation funding: +10 blocks per normalized unit

vectors.name: seq_post_straddle
vectors.note: funded 10 blocks before activation with n=10 releases exactly at activation

vectors.name: seq_multi_300tick
vectors.note: in a 300-tick segment one normalized unit = 2 blocks

vectors.name: mat_post_fund_Ha
vectors.note: coinbase created in the last 600-tick block matures after exactly 1,000 one-minute blocks

vectors.name: mat_post_c1001000
vectors.note: post-activation coinbase: 60,000 ticks = 1,000 blocks

vectors.name: mat_post_straddle
vectors.note: coinbase 100 blocks before activation (60,000 ticks) matures exactly at activation

vectors.name: mat_multi_300tick
vectors.note: 60,000 ticks = 200 blocks in a 300-tick segment

vectors.name: lock_multi_300tick
vectors.note: strictness where 600*L (30,060,000) is exactly a block tick inside a 300-tick segment

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_bip54_h_plus_2
vectors.note: BIP-54 template stamping nLockTime = height - 1 with a non-final input sequence, as it lands in block H_a + 2 (1,000,002) where the value is 1,000,001. Below H_a + 1 the pre-activation rule governs and block H_a rejects the stamp; from H_a + 1 the exemption makes it final in every block, which is what keeps that template valid. The check at 1,000,010 is the endpoint of that range and the sharp one: T(1,000,010) = 600,000,600 equals the boundary 600 * 1,000,001 exactly, so the strict > is what would reject it, while lock_noncoinbase_bip54_twin pins the identical fields as false there. Without the exemption the raw predicate would call 1,000,002..1,000,010 non-final -- T(1,000,002) = 600,000,120 is far short -- recovering only at 1,000,011.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_bip54_h_plus_1
vectors.note: The other half of the BIP-54 pair: block H_a + 1 carries nLockTime = 1,000,000. Below the gate the field binds -- at block H_a itself 1,000,000 is not below 1,000,000 and the input sequence is non-final, so the pre-activation rule rejects it -- while the exemption makes it final at H_a + 1, where the raw tick predicate 600,000,060 > 600,000,000 would also have cleared it. Pinned so the handover is visible: the same fields are non-final exactly one block earlier.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_time_mode
vectors.note: Time-mode nLockTime (>= LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD), evaluated with the harness default nBlockTime = 0, so the pre-activation time-mode arm reports non-final everywhere at or below H_a. The value is only a time-mode marker: as a timestamp it is in 1989, so a real lock-time cutoff would make it final by the ordinary rule; timeModeVectors holds the rows with a realistic cutoff. The exemption covers the time-mode arm too, but only from H_a + 1.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_zero_sequence
vectors.note: nSequence 0x00000000 with a height-mode locktime naming 1,000,011: the raw tick predicate, without the exemption, would only clear it at 1,000,111. 'Whatever the nSequence' is the arm pinned here -- the exemption does not read it, and it starts at H_a + 1 like every other upgraded rule.

vectors.name: lock_noncoinbase_bip54_twin
vectors.note: Non-coinbase twin of lock_coinbase_bip54_h_plus_2: identical fields, only the subject differs, and the raw predicate binds unchanged. This is what makes the exemption a restriction on scope rather than a relaxation of the two predicates for everyone.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_pre_activation_binds
vectors.note: The exemption is a post-upgrade rule, not an unconditional property of coinbases: with nLockTime = 1 and a non-final sequence this coinbase is non-final at blocks 0 and 1 and final from block 2, all well below H_a. A harness that bypassed every coinbase would report release 0 here -- which is exactly the defect this family shipped with.

vectors.name: lock_height_mode_max
vectors.note: The largest height-mode nLockTime (LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD - 1). It is compared in ticks, T(b) > 600 * 499,999,999 = 299,999,999,400 (a product that needs more than 32 bits), and releases at block 500,000,000 on the 600-tick schedule. An implementation that treated this value as time-mode would never release it here, where no block time is supplied; lock_time_mode_min in timeModeVectors is the value one higher.

vectors.name: seq_post_n0_fund_Ha
vectors.note: relativeLock 0 with BIP 68 enforced (version 2, disable flag clear): mature in the funding block itself, T(b) - T(fundingBlock) >= 0, and false only below it (the underflow guard). The mempool check at tip 999,999 is the next block being the funding block.

vectors.name: seq_post_cross_Ha_n2
vectors.note: funded one block before H_a with n=2: T(999,999) = 599,999,400, so the lock needs tick 600,000,600 = block 1,000,010. The 1,200 ticks are block H_a (600) plus ten 1-minute blocks; seq_post_straddle stops at H_a and never mixes the two intervals. Both wrong forms accept it early: the block count at block 1,000,001 (1,000,001 - 999,999 = 2), and T(tip) + tau(tip) = 600,000,600 in the mempool at tip = H_a. seq_post_fund_Ha_n1 catches those two as well. Only this row catches converting n into a block count with a single interval: that of the block after funding releases it at 1,000,001, that of the spend block at 1,000,019.

vectors.name: mat_post_mempool_tip_Ha
vectors.note: coinbase created 99 blocks before H_a: T(999,901) = 599,940,600, so it matures at tick 600,000,600 = block 1,000,010. The mempool check at tip = H_a evaluates block H_a + 1 with T(H_a + 1) = 600,000,060 from the schedule, 59,460 ticks after creation: not spendable. Both wrong forms accept it there: the block count (1,000,001 - 999,901 = 100) and T(tip) + tau(tip) = 600,000,600.

timeModeVectors.name: lock_coinbase_time_mode_above
timeModeVectors.note: Time-mode nLockTime 2,000,000,001 (2033), far above the supplied cutoff of 1,800,000,000 and above any cutoff a chain can have around the upgrade, with a non-final input sequence. At H_a the upgrade is not active, the time-mode arm runs and the lock is not below the cutoff: the coinbase is non-final and block H_a is invalid. At H_a + 1 the same coinbase is final, and only the exemption can be what frees it: the ordinary rule still rejects it, as lock_noncoinbase_time_mode_twin shows. The value is far past activation on purpose. In a node the cutoff at H_a + 1 is the median-time-past that activated the upgrade, so a lock just above 1,800,000,000 would be final there by the ordinary rule and would not test the exemption.

timeModeVectors.name: lock_coinbase_time_mode_equal
timeModeVectors.note: Pins the strict comparison at H_a, not the exemption: nLockTime equal to the supplied cutoff is still non-final there (final iff lockTime < cutoff), which is what tells < from <=. The result at H_a + 1 is by exemption in this harness, which holds the cutoff constant; under a real post-activation cutoff, which is above 1,800,000,000, the ordinary rule would make it final as well.

timeModeVectors.name: lock_coinbase_time_mode_below
timeModeVectors.note: The other side of the strict comparison at H_a: nLockTime one second below the supplied cutoff is final at H_a by the ordinary time-mode rule, with no exemption involved, and still final after it. Because the vector supplies the same cutoff at every block, the release block is 0; the check that matters is the one at H_a.

timeModeVectors.name: lock_noncoinbase_time_mode_twin
timeModeVectors.note: Non-coinbase twin of lock_coinbase_time_mode_above: identical fields and cutoff, only the subject differs. It stays non-final above H_a, in blocks and in the mempool, so the exemption does not relax the time-mode arm for anyone else; with nLockTime 2,000,000,001 that holds for any cutoff a chain can have around the upgrade, not only the one supplied. Under a constant cutoff below nLockTime no block releases it, so releaseBlock is null.

timeModeVectors.name: lock_time_mode_min
timeModeVectors.note: The smallest time-mode nLockTime (LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD): compared against the supplied cutoff of 1,800,000,000 and so final at every block, where lock_height_mode_max in `vectors`, one lower, is height-mode and not final below block 500,000,000.
